current.text: He says he has no restrictions, and the GM expects him ready for opening night.
He missed a preseason game with an ankle injury. The expert does not see the ankle as a worry.
He had very high usage in the first half of a preseason game.
The high preseason usage eases concerns about his recovery.
Experts expect Rick Carlisle to manage his minutes early in the season, with some missed games and a ramp-up period.
Experts expect him to sit or be limited in some back-to-backs early in the season.
About 30 minutes is expected in games without a back-to-back. One expert does not expect 34 minutes per game over the full season.
Experts expect rust early: lower efficiency on his percentages and possibly a little less usage. His two-point percentage could drop from about 59 to 57.
Compensation injuries after the torn Achilles are the main health worry.
Experts expect him to be back to full strength around January, and near his best by the fantasy playoffs.

Experts call his Yahoo rank of 10 too early for category leagues. They see him as an end of round 1 to middle of round 2 pick, in the 14 to 20 range. His range of outcomes is the widest in round one, from 8th at best to 55th at worst.
In an auction, Josh would not pay more than 35 USD for him.
He is a projected starter next to Nembhard, Nesmith, Siakam and Zubac. McConnell and Nembhard can handle the ball when he is managed.
Indiana is projected to win 46 to 48 games and get a top-six seed in the East.
Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks with a March 28 end, which is not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He tore his Achilles in the June 2025 NBA Finals and missed the whole 2025-26 season. He also had a case of shingles.
His assists are elite. He is always a threat to lead the league in assists.
He is an assist source, not a high scorer or high usage player. Draft him early if you want assists. One expert says taking him in round one pushes a team toward punting points.
He is a great shooter. In his last full season he made just under 40% of his threes.
His steals and FG% have been good. Finishing at the rim on two-point shots is a strength.
He picks apart confused defenses and commits very few turnovers for his playmaking load.
How he plays shapes the fantasy value of every other Pacer.
He is worth clearly more in category leagues than in Yahoo points leagues, where he is not a top 10 player even when healthy.
None of his categories is weak, so he fits any build.

note: His assists are elite (9.4 projected, z +3.3) and none of his categories is weak, so he fits any build. But the experts agree that Yahoo's rank of 10 and value of 49 USD are too high for a player coming off a torn Achilles who is likely to be managed early. Josh's ceiling is 35 USD and ESPN's average cost is 39.4 USD, so a price in the mid-to-high 30s matches the round 2 value the experts see. His playoff schedule is only 3-4-3 games, so his late-season ramp-up helps less in our format. Early in the season, check his minutes in games without a back-to-back, how Carlisle handles back-to-backs before Thanksgiving, and whether his FG% shows rust.
